title: Wall Street Wiped Out: Massive Tech Rout Pushes Dow and S&P 500 Into Correction
snippet: A brutal sell-off engulfed Wall Street on Friday as deepening anxieties over AI financing and safety sent tech heavyweights into a tailspin, pushing major indices deep into correction territory.
content:
Wall Street suffered a devastating blow on Friday as a relentless market sell-off accelerated, driven by mounting fears over artificial intelligence financing and safety risks. Despite high hopes surrounding Anthropic's high-profile debut earlier in the week, panic swept across trading desks, driving major benchmarks down sharply and dragging the tech-heavy Nasdaq into negative territory for the year.

Indices Plunge into Correction Territory

The Dow Jones Industrial Average plummeted 1.9%, breaking down below the 50,000 milestone. Meanwhile, the benchmark S&P 500 tumbled 3.6%. Both indices officially closed in correction territory, having fallen more than 10% from their recent record peaks. The turmoil was felt most acutely in the Nasdaq Composite, which plunged nearly 5.3% as investors fled high-growth assets.

Semiconductors Lead the Slaughter

Chipmakers and hardware giants bore the brunt of the market's risk-off pivot. Artificial intelligence powerhouse Nvidia extended its recent losses with a eye-watering 14% drop. Industry peers AMD, Broadcom, and Micron also posted double-digit declines. The scale of the collapse was stark across the board: 71 of the 101 stocks in the Nasdaq-100 are now in bear market territory, including all 20 semiconductor and memory chip equities in the index.

Broader Markets Feel the Heat

Even newly minted market darling Anthropic felt the chill. A day after its record-breaking debut, Anthropic shares sank 8%, though they managed to remain slightly above their $83 IPO price as the company faces its first real test of market resilience.

The flight from risk spread far beyond equities. Gold futures dropped nearly 4%, while Bitcoin broke key support levels to fall below $59,000, touching its lowest price since July.
